exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation
exercises.instructions: Which description matches first-generation programming languages in the slides?
options: Machine language consisting of binary code used by computers
Assembly language using readable processor-specific instructions
Third-generation language source code
Java bytecode for the JVM
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slides identify machine language (binary code) as the first generation and describe it as processor-specific.

exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation (2)
exercises.instructions: Which statements about machine language, assembly language and 3GLs are supported by the slides? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Machine language is binary code.
Assembly language is more readable than machine language.
Assembly language is processor-specific.
3GL code is described as processor-independent.
Assembly language is described as processor-independent code.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide labels machine language as first generation, assembly as second generation and more readable but processor-specific, and 3GL as processor-independent. The added statement is incorrect: Assembly language is described as processor-independent code.

exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation (3)
exercises.instructions: How do the slides describe assembly language?
options: More readable, processor-specific code
Binary code that is processor-independent
Source code interpreted directly on any platform
Bytecode for the Java Virtual Machine
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: Assembly language is presented as second-generation, more readable processor-specific code.

exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation (4)
exercises.instructions: Which of the following is explicitly given as an example of a 3GL?
options: Java
Machine code
Intel binary instructions
A processor-specific assembly instruction
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: Java appears in the slide’s list of third-generation language examples.

exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation (5)
exercises.instructions: Which languages are explicitly named as examples of compiled languages in the slides? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: C
JavaScript
Python
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The compiled-language slide lists C and C++ as examples; JavaScript and Python appear as interpreted-language examples.

exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation (6)
exercises.instructions: Which characteristics of Java are listed on the slide titled “Why is Java so popular?” Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.

Object-oriented
Distributed
Robust
Multithreaded
Secure
Fast

hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.

exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation (7)
exercises.instructions: According to the comparison table, which language is marked as platform independent?
options: Java
Neither C++ nor Java
Both C++ and Java
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The comparison table marks C++ as not platform independent and Java as platform independent.

exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation (8)
exercises.instructions: Which Java/C++ comparison statements match the coursework table? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Both are marked as object-oriented.
C++ syntax is based on C.
Java syntax is based on C++.
Java is marked as suitable for system programming.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The table says both are object-oriented, C++ syntax is based on C, and Java syntax is based on C++; it marks C++ yes and Java no for system programming.

exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation (9)
exercises.instructions: What does the coursework identify as the key platform-independence benefit of Java compared with C++?
options: Java is marked platform independent, while C++ is not.
Java does not need a runtime environment.
Java source code is converted directly to processor-specific binary code only once.
Java can only run on desktop computers.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The comparison table highlights platform independence as the distinguishing characteristic.

exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation (10)
exercises.instructions: Which advantages of a compiled language are listed in the coursework? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Compile-time checks
Portable source code
Fast execution because binary code can run directly
Source code is not readable at the target platform
The compiled-language slide says a separate interpreter is needed on every target platform.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: All four are listed as compiled-language advantages on the slide. The added statement is incorrect: The compiled-language slide says a separate interpreter is needed on every target platform.

exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation (11)
exercises.instructions: Which disadvantages of a compiled language are listed? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Platform-dependent binary code must be distributed to each target platform.
Changing code for testing requires recompilation.
There are no compile-time checks.
An interpreter is required on every target system.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The compiled-language slide lists platform dependence and the need to recompile after code changes. The other statements are listed as interpreted-language disadvantages.

exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation (12)
exercises.instructions: Which speed description is assigned to interpreted languages in the comparison?
options: Slow
Fast
Medium
Not stated
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The interpreted-language slide lists speed as slow.

exercises.title: Programming Languages and Language Translation (13)
exercises.instructions: Which disadvantages of interpreted languages are explicitly listed? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: No compile-time checks
An interpreter is needed on each system where the program runs
The source code is readable on the target platform
The program runs faster than compiled binary code
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slides list no compile-time checks, the need for an interpreter on each system, and readable source code at the target platform. They describe interpreted execution as slow.

exercises.title: The Java Platform and Your First Java Program
exercises.instructions: What is the Java API according to the coursework?
options: Java libraries; API stands for Application Programming Interface
The Java command-line compiler
The binary bytecode file
An IDE workbench
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide expands API as Application Programming Interface and identifies it as Java libraries.

exercises.title: The Java Platform and Your First Java Program (2)
exercises.instructions: What combination hides the underlying platform in the Java platform diagram?
options: Java API and Java Virtual Machine
JDK and IDE
Scanner and System.in
Compiler and source editor
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide says the Java API and JVM hide the underlying platform, making Java programs platform independent.

exercises.title: The Java Platform and Your First Java Program (3)
exercises.instructions: Which statements about the JRE are supported by the slides? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: JRE means Java Runtime Environment.
It consists of the JVM and Java API.
It is needed to run Java programs in bytecode.
It is the full developer toolset that includes compile and debug tools.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The JRE is defined as JVM + Java API and is needed to run bytecode programs. The JDK is the set that adds development tools.

exercises.title: The Java Platform and Your First Java Program (4)
exercises.instructions: Which statements about the JDK match the coursework? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: JDK means Java Development Kit.
It contains the JRE.
It includes tools such as compiling and debugging.
The API reference documentation is described as optional.
The JDK is described as containing no development tools such as compiling or debugging.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide lists all four statements and summarizes the JDK as the JRE plus additional tools and documentation. The added statement is incorrect: The JDK is described as containing no development tools such as compiling or debugging.

exercises.title: The Java Platform and Your First Java Program (5)
exercises.instructions: How is an IDE described in the coursework?
options: A workbench application for developers
A Java bytecode file
The Java runtime environment
A processor-specific assembly language
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide defines an IDE as a workbench application for developers.

exercises.title: The Java Platform and Your First Java Program (6)
exercises.instructions: Which statements about IDEs are explicitly made? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: They are workbench applications for developers.
They are often usable for development in multiple programming languages.
IntelliJ can assist when writing, building and running code.
An IDE replaces the Java Virtual Machine.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slides describe IDEs as developer workbenches, often multi-language, and say IntelliJ assists with writing, building and running code. It does not replace the JVM.

exercises.title: The Java Platform and Your First Java Program (7)
exercises.instructions: What is the file extension for Java source code?
options: .java
.class
java
javac
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The first-program slide specifies the .java extension for source code files.

exercises.title: The Java Platform and Your First Java Program (8)
exercises.instructions: Which command is identified as the JDK command-line compiler?
options: javac
java
jre
jvm
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The compile slide states that javac is the command-line compiler bundled with the JDK.

exercises.title: The Java Platform and Your First Java Program (9)
exercises.instructions: Which command starts the JVM and executes bytecode according to the slides?
options: java
javac
Scanner
System.out
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The run slide explains that java is the JDK or JRE command that starts the JVM and executes bytecode.

exercises.title: The Java Platform and Your First Java Program (10)
exercises.instructions: Which statements correctly describe the basic Java program workflow? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Write source code.
Compile the source code.
Run the program.
Run the source file before writing it.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide presents the sequence write source code, compile, and run.

exercises.title: The Java Platform and Your First Java Program (11)
exercises.instructions: Which facts about compiling and running are stated in the slides? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: The generated bytecode file has the .class extension.
The javac command compiles source code.
The java command executes bytecode by starting the JVM.
The java command is described as the compiler.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slides distinguish javac for compiling from java for starting the JVM and executing bytecode.

exercises.title: The Java Platform and Your First Java Program (12)
exercises.instructions: Which facts about comments and the main method are supported by the code walkthrough? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Text between /* and */ is a comment.
Text preceded by // is a comment.
Comments are ignored by the compiler and can document code.
The main method is the starting point of a Java application.
The slides say comment text is executed as part of the program.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The code walkthrough explicitly describes both comment forms and identifies main as the application starting point. The added statement is incorrect: The slides say comment text is executed as part of the program.

exercises.title: Programming Algorithms and Flowcharts
exercises.instructions: What is an algorithm according to the slides?
options: Steps to perform a task
A Java class containing attributes
A collection of binary instructions for a processor
A method that must return a value
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The coursework defines an algorithm as steps to perform a task.

exercises.title: Programming Algorithms and Flowcharts (2)
exercises.instructions: What two activities does the coursework identify as programming? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Designing an algorithm to perform a task
Encoding the algorithm in a programming language so a computer can do the task
Choosing a processor-specific binary format before designing the task
Writing an IDE before defining the algorithm
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide says programming is designing an algorithm and encoding it in a programming language for the computer.

exercises.title: Programming Algorithms and Flowcharts (3)
exercises.instructions: Which actions are listed as typical actions in an algorithm? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Ask input
Produce output
Test
Repeat
Compute
The typical algorithm actions explicitly exclude both testing and repetition.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The robot-algorithm conclusion lists asking input, producing output, testing, repeating and computing. The added statement is incorrect: The typical algorithm actions explicitly exclude both testing and repetition.

exercises.title: Programming Algorithms and Flowcharts (4)
exercises.instructions: What does the robot example teach about the detail of an algorithm?
options: Actions must be elaborated to the level understood by the robot.
Actions should be kept vague so the robot can decide.
Only output steps need to be specified.
A robot can infer missing steps from the task title.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide emphasizes elaborating actions to the level understood by the robot.

exercises.title: Programming Algorithms and Flowcharts (5)
exercises.instructions: Which elements are identified in the simple sum algorithm? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Input and output (I/O)
Intermediate results stored in variables
Computing using variables
A constructor for a Sum object
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The sum algorithm slide labels input/output, intermediate values in variables and computation using variables.

exercises.title: Programming Algorithms and Flowcharts (6)
exercises.instructions: In the sum example, what is the role of the variable `sum`?
options: It stores the result computed from the two input values.
It stores the keyboard object.
It stores the text of the prompt.
It determines which package is imported.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The algorithm reads two numbers, computes their sum using variables and displays that intermediate result.

exercises.title: Programming Algorithms and Flowcharts (7)
exercises.instructions: When transforming the algorithm into Java, which statements are explicitly taught? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Each algorithm step becomes a Java statement terminated by a semicolon.
System.out.print("text") displays output.
keyboard.nextInt() reads an integer from the keyboard.
The assignment operator places the value on the left side into the right side.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slides state that each step becomes a semicolon-terminated Java statement, show System.out.print for output and keyboard.nextInt for input, and explain assignment as copying the right-hand value to the left-hand variable.

exercises.title: Programming Algorithms and Flowcharts (8)
exercises.instructions: Which flowchart ideas are illustrated by the pizza-order robot? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: A loop repeats a sequence of steps several times.
A test selects different actions depending on its result.
The algorithm has a start and an end.
All actions are performed only once and in a fixed straight line.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The flowchart annotations identify a repeated sequence as a loop, branching as a test, and the start/end of the process.

exercises.title: Expressions, Statements, Blocks and Scope
exercises.instructions: What is an expression in the coursework definition?
options: A construct made of literals, variables, operators and/or method calls that evaluates to one value
A basic instruction that always ends a program
A group of statements enclosed in curly braces
A declaration of a variable type only
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide defines an expression as a construct of literals, variables, operators and/or method calls that evaluates to a single value.

exercises.title: Expressions, Statements, Blocks and Scope (2)
exercises.instructions: Which item is described as a basic instruction?
options: A statement
A literal
A variable scope
A class
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The statement slide labels a statement as a basic instruction.

exercises.title: Expressions, Statements, Blocks and Scope (3)
exercises.instructions: Which statement types are explicitly listed in the coursework? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Declaration
Assignment
Method call
Compound statement for flow control
A declaration is not included among the statement types in the slides.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The statement-types slide lists declaration, assignment, method call and compound statements. The added statement is incorrect: A declaration is not included among the statement types in the slides.

exercises.title: Expressions, Statements, Blocks and Scope (4)
exercises.instructions: Which statement is a declaration statement in the example?
options: double a;
a = 15 * Math.PI;
System.out.println(a);
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide labels `double a;` as a declaration statement.

exercises.title: Expressions, Statements, Blocks and Scope (5)
exercises.instructions: How are single statements terminated in the coursework examples?
options: With a semicolon
With a comma
With a colon
With a closing curly brace only
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The statement slide explicitly says single statements are terminated with a semicolon.

exercises.title: Expressions, Statements, Blocks and Scope (6)
exercises.instructions: Which statements about a code block are correct according to the slides? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: A block is a group of statements.
Statements in a block are enclosed in a pair of curly braces.
A block can be used anywhere a simple statement is allowed.
A block can contain only one statement.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The block slide defines a block as grouped statements enclosed in curly braces and says it can be used wherever a simple statement is allowed.

exercises.title: Expressions, Statements, Blocks and Scope (7)
exercises.instructions: What is the recommended indentation convention for a new code block?
options: Indent statements an extra level within each new block.
Indent all statements at the same level.
Indent only declarations.
Indent only the closing brace.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The code convention slide says to indent statements an extra level within each new code block.

exercises.title: Expressions, Statements, Blocks and Scope (8)
exercises.instructions: Which code-formatting recommendations are stated? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Indent statements one extra level inside each new block.
Indent when continuing a statement on a new line.
Use the IDE reformat command when desired.
Remove indentation from nested blocks.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slides give both indentation recommendations and show Code > Reformat Code with Ctrl-Alt-L.

exercises.title: Expressions, Statements, Blocks and Scope (9)
exercises.instructions: What does variable scope mean?
options: The program region where a variable is known and can be used
The number of values a variable can store
The data type of a variable
The number of statements in a block
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide defines scope as the program region where a variable is known and usable.

exercises.title: Expressions, Statements, Blocks and Scope (10)
exercises.instructions: Which statements describe the scope of a variable declared in a block? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: It is known within the block where it is declared.
It is known in nested code blocks.
Its scope starts at the declaration line.
Its scope ends at the closing curly brace of the declaring block.
A variable declared inside a block remains known throughout the entire program, outside that block.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: All four details appear on the variable-scope slide. The added statement is incorrect: A variable declared inside a block remains known throughout the entire program, outside that block.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch
exercises.instructions: When does an `if` block execute?
options: When its logical condition is true
When its logical condition is false
Once regardless of the condition
Only when an `else` block is present
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The if slide says the block is executed only when the logical expression is true.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (2)
exercises.instructions: Which statements describe an `if...else` statement? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: The if-block executes when the logical expression is true.
The else-block executes when the logical expression is false.
It provides a branch for both truth outcomes.
Both blocks always execute.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slides say the if-block is used for true and the else-block for false; they are alternative branches.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (3)
exercises.instructions: What is the best-practice recommendation for an `if` statement?
options: Always use a code block after an if.
Never use curly braces.
Always use an else branch.
Use a switch statement instead.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The if-syntax slide explicitly recommends always using a code block after an if.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (4)
exercises.instructions: What is the stated advantage of the `if ... else if` structure over deeply nested if statements?
options: It gives a simpler structure.
It always executes every branch.
It returns a value.
It eliminates conditions.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slides contrast complex deep nesting with the simpler if-else-if structure.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (5)
exercises.instructions: Which recommendations about if/else formatting appear in the slides? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Use a code block after if.
Use a code block after else.
When an else is followed by a single if statement, the slides show that a simple statement without a block is acceptable.
Always nest each else-if branch inside another pair of braces.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slides recommend blocks after if and else, while identifying a single if after else as a case where a simple statement (no extra block) is best practice.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (6)
exercises.instructions: What is the conditional operator syntax shown in the slides?
options: op1 ? op2 : op3
op1 : op2 ? op3
if (op1) then op2 else op3
op1 && op2 || op3
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The conditional operator table gives the usage `op1 ? op2 : op3`.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (7)
exercises.instructions: Which statements distinguish the conditional operator from an if/else statement? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: The conditional operator is also called a ternary operator.
Its first operand must be a boolean expression.
It yields op2 when op1 is true and op3 otherwise.
It is an expression that returns a value.
An if/else statement is described as not returning a value.
The slides say the conditional operator does not return a value.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: All five statements are stated on the conditional-operator slide. The added statement is incorrect: The slides say the conditional operator does not return a value.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (8)
exercises.instructions: What is the purpose of a switch statement in the coursework?
options: To test equality against multiple values
To repeat a block while a condition is true
To declare a variable
To convert a double into an int
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The switch slide describes it as a way to test equality against multiple values.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (9)
exercises.instructions: Which selector types are explicitly named in the switch syntax slide? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Integral types such as int and long
String
double only
boolean only
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide labels the switch value as an integral type (int, long...) or String.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (10)
exercises.instructions: In the traditional switch syntax, when do statements for a matching case stop executing?
options: At the next break statement
At the next case label, always
Immediately after the first statement
Only at the end of the switch
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The syntax slide says statements execute until the next break; without a break, following case statements execute too.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (11)
exercises.instructions: Which statements about `break` and `default` in the traditional switch are correct? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Without break, execution can fall through into statements of the next case.
The default label is optional.
If no case matches, default statements execute when a default is present.
A default branch must always be present in every traditional switch.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide explains fall-through, the optional default label, and execution of default if no case matches.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (12)
exercises.instructions: What does “fall through” mean in the traditional switch example?
options: Execution continues through subsequent case statements until a break.
The switch skips every matching case.
The switch returns a value from the first case.
The compiler ignores all case labels.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slides explicitly label the behavior as fall through until a break.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (13)
exercises.instructions: Which features are shown for the simplified switch syntax introduced in the coursework? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Multiple values can be listed in one case.
The arrow `->` replaces the traditional colon in the shown form.
No break is necessary.
There is no fall-through in the shown simplified form.
The simplified switch form requires a break after every case and uses fall-through.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide labels the simplified switch as supporting multiple values per case and says no break and no fall-through are needed. The added statement is incorrect: The simplified switch form requires a break after every case and uses fall-through.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (14)
exercises.instructions: When using a simplified switch as an expression, when is `default` mandatory according to the slides?
options: When all possible cases are not covered
Whenever a case contains more than one value
Only when a break is used
Never
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide says a default branch is mandatory for a switch expression if not all possible cases are covered.

exercises.title: Conditional Execution and Switch (15)
exercises.instructions: When a simplified switch expression uses a block with multiple statements, what does the coursework require? Select all correct answers. More than one answer is correct.
options: Use a block for the case body.
Use `yield` before the value to be returned.
The yielded value becomes the switch expression result.
Use `break` to return the value.
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
exercises.explanation: The slide says that when using a block with multiple statements, precede the value to be returned with `yield`.

exercises.title: Loops: while, do-while, for, break and continue
exercises.instructions: What is an iteration according to the loop slides?
options: A code block executed repeatedly
A variable declaration inside a class
A single value returned by an expression
A statement that imports a class
hints: Use the definitions, distinctions and examples stated in the coursework.
